scores.claim_text: HEICO is a leading supplier/distributor/integrator of military aircraft parts to DoD and defense prime contractors including F-16 support.
scores.M_value: n_awards=5462, total_amount=$186.78M obligated across DoD; top recipients are HEICO subsidiaries: Robertson Fuel Systems LLC (multiple $10M-$42M IDIQ awards for crashworthy external fuel system kits, internal auxiliary fuel systems, AMATTS), Santa Barbara Infrared (infrared scene projectors $6.8M-$11.7M, training simulation), Radiant Power Corp (military warning lights), Intelligent Devices LLC (Maxwell talker comm equipment). Awards include explicit Naval Air Warfare Center, U.S. Army aviation (W58RGZ Aviation & Missile Command), USAF (FA-prefixed) contracts. Multiple IDIQs reference Government of Japan FMS — confirming foreign military sales claim.
scores.interpretation: Strong, broad-based DoD presence across HEICO's named subsidiaries spanning multiple service branches (Navy, Army, USAF) and FMS to allied nations. Entity resolution required (search by parent 'HEICO' does not surface most contracts; the subsidiaries Robertson Fuel Systems, Santa Barbara Infrared, Radiant Power Corp, Intelligent Devices, ASTRO MET, etc. are the actual recipient_uniqueid). The contract mix (crashworthy fuel kits, infrared simulation, warning lights, talkers, FMS) is fully consistent with the FSG/ETG product descriptions in Item 1. F-16-specific tail-spend not separately broken out but the diversified DoD obligation pattern corroborates the broad 'leading supplier' framing. Mode A PASSES cleanly.

scores.claim_text: ETG derived ~51% of FY2025 net sales from US/foreign military, prime defense contractors, and satellite/spacecraft manufacturers.
scores.M_value: Direct DoD-Electronic search: n_awards=41, total_amount=$26.7M (Robertson Fuel Systems crashworthy systems $12.3M + Santa Barbara IR $11.7M dominate). Counterparty disclosure: Lockheed (CIK 0000936468) 0 hits; Northrop (CIK 0001133421) 0 hits; Boeing (CIK 0000012927) 0 hits; L3Harris (CIK 0000202058) 0 hits. Aggregate DoD presence is large ($186.8M parent-roll) but Electronic-segment subset is narrower than Item 1 framing suggests.
scores.interpretation: Mode A: DoD obligations exist and are real, but the $26.7M direct ETG-tagged subset is modest relative to ETG's segment revenue (~30% of $4.485B parent = ~$1.35B). The 51% defense/space figure relies heavily on (a) US defense prime sub-tier sales (commercial-off-the-shelf hi-rel components flowing into prime BOMs), and (b) commercial+defense satellite/spacecraft buyers (SpaceX, ULA, Maxar, Northrop Space, satellite primes) that may not appear under HEICO's prime-recipient name on USAspending. Mode B (counterparty disclosure): 0 mentions in any of the four largest primes' filings is fully expected per heuristic 7 — HEICO's sub-tier hi-rel passives/connectors per prime would each be well below 10% disclosure threshold. NOT a SEVE. The MOD downgrade reflects the gap between (a) the 51% framing's prime-defense weight vs (b) directly verifiable federal obligations being concentrated in a few named subs, not a fabrication.

scores.claim_text: 107 acquisitions since 1990 under a 'disciplined acquisition strategy'; FY2025 acquisitions consumed $629.8M including 4 acqs (SVM, Millennium, Rosen, Gables) excluded from FY2025 ICFR assessment.
scores.M_value: mean_coherence=0.8375, signal=COHERENT_ROLLUP, n_low_coherence=0, n_revenue_synthetic=0. Per-acq scores: Wencor 0.95 (highest — pure PMA aftermarket extension), Millennium 0.85, Gables 0.85, Exxelia 0.85, Axillon 0.85, EthosEnergy 0.85, Rosen 0.75, SVM 0.75. All 8 land in high_coherence band. Aggregate rollup is tightly bound to FAA-PMA + defense electronics thesis across two segments.
scores.interpretation: Unlike incoherent rollups (e.g., quantum-computing parent buying SAR satellites + atomic clocks + foundries), HEICO's acquisition stream is highly disciplined within two clear lanes: (FSG) FAA-PMA aftermarket parts, MRO, avionics repair, military aircraft parts; (ETG) hi-rel passives/interconnects, capacitors, power supplies for defense/space. Mode B aggregate coherence (0.8375) does NOT trip the rollup-incoherence signal. The disclosed exclusion of 4 acquisitions from FY2025 ICFR assessment is the standard SEC-permitted first-year carve-out (combined 2.3% assets, 1.6% sales — well within the typical safe-harbor), not a flag. PASS.

scores.M_value: 8-K filings: 50 total 8-Ks confirmed (regular cadence; 12/18/2025 + 12/22/2025 8-Ks bracket the 10-K). Insider sales: n_form4_filings=20, n_total_sales=7, n_total_sale_value=$57.5M aggregated, but most sales NOT proximate to budget events. n_proximate_sales=1 (Julie Neitzel, director, $150,748 sale on 2026-04-15 = 13 days BEFORE FY27 J-Book release on 2026-04-28). Discretionary (non-10b5-1). signal=PROXIMATE_DISCRETIONARY.
scores.interpretation: Mode A confirms standard debt structure / 8-K cadence consistent with 10-K disclosure. Mode B (insider_vs_calendar): the algorithm flags a single discretionary director sale 13 days before the FY27 J-Book release — but the magnitude is small ($150k) and from a non-executive director (Neitzel), not a CEO/CFO/co-CEO. Total aggregate sales of $57.5M across 20 Form 4s over 24 months is unremarkable for a $30B+ market-cap aerospace name with deeply embedded founder-family share concentration (Mendelson family Class A). The PROXIMATE_DISCRETIONARY flag is technical but materially small; not a clustering pattern. Mild MOD given the framework flagged it. Not RED/SEVE — single small sale, single non-exec director.

scores.M_value: EPA FRS (FL only): 3 facilities — HEICO Aerospace at 7875 NW 64th St Miami; HEICO Aerospace Corp at 3000 Taft St Hollywood (corporate HQ); HEICO Corporation at 7875/7900 NW 64 Street Miami. OSHA: 4 establishments — HEICO Component Repair Group (Miami FL, 139 emp, NAICS 488190 aircraft repair); HEICO Aerospace (Hollywood FL, 169 emp, NAICS 336412 aircraft engine parts mfg); HEICO Corporation (Hollywood FL, 80 emp, same NAICS); Astroseal Products Mfg Corp / HEICO Corp (Chester CT, 22 emp, NAICS 331420 aircraft wire). Total registered employees in OSHA file: 410 (FL-3, CT-1). signal=REGISTERED_EMPLOYER.
scores.interpretation: Both registries independently corroborate HEICO's facility footprint at the principal Hollywood FL (3000 Taft St) HQ and Miami FL (7875 NW 64 St) operations. NAICS codes (336412 aircraft engine parts, 488190 aircraft repair, 331420 aircraft wire) directly match the 10-K's FSG product descriptions. The 19-state US footprint per segment is much larger than the 4 OSHA hits returned by 'HEICO' word-boundary match — but this is expected per heuristic 6 (name-variant fragility): the vast majority of HEICO's footprint operates under acquired-entity brand names (Robertson Fuel Systems AZ, Santa Barbara Infrared CA, Wencor GA, Exxelia France, etc.) not 'HEICO'. Top-line EPA + OSHA hits at the disclosed HQ addresses fully confirm the disclosure. PASS.

scores.claim_text: HEICO holds ~20,000 FAA PMAs, adds 400-550 PMAs per year; no material patents; relies primarily on trade secrets.
scores.M_value: USPTO HEICO: 6 granted patents (all 'Heico Befestigungstechnik GmbH', a German bolt/washer fastener company — UNRELATED to HEICO Corporation aerospace; F16B fasteners CPC, locking washers/expansion bolts/bolting tools). HEICO Corporation (exact assignee): 1 PCT application from 2010 (aircraft cabin temperature sensor filter), never advanced to grant. Exxelia: 1 granted patent (NiZnCu ferrite for VHF antennas, 2025-10-28). Wencor: 0 patents. Heico Befestigungstechnik GmbH is a separate German company; not the issuer.
scores.interpretation: Patent search RESULT IS THE CLAIM. HEICO explicitly states it has 'no material patents' for its core PMA techniques and uses trade secrets instead. Mode A USPTO query confirms: HEICO Corporation as an assignee has effectively 0 granted patents (1 abandoned PCT app). The 6 granted patents under 'HEICO' (Befestigungstechnik) belong to an UNRELATED German fastener firm. The Exxelia subsidiary has 1 granted (passive component physics). Per heuristic 8 (patent rubric), normally absence-of-patents would be a flag, but here the company AFFIRMATIVELY tells you they don't patent — and a non-OEM PMA business legitimately operates this way (reverse-engineering OEM parts under FAA approval relies on FAA-protected drawings + manufacturing process know-how, not patent claims). The 20,000 PMA count is FAA-registry verifiable (not in scope of USPTO) and is a separate regulatory artifact. PASS — Mode A confirms the company's self-description rather than contradicting it.
